results.title: Tokio - An asynchronous runtime for Rust
results.content: Tokio is an asynchronous runtime for the Rust programming language. It provides the building blocks needed for writing network applications. It gives the flexibility to target a wide range of systems, from large servers with dozens of cores to small embedded devices.

results.title: tokio - Rust
results.content: Tokio is a runtime for writing reliable asynchronous applications with Rust. It provides I/O, networking, scheduling, timers, and more. The core primitives include async and await syntax, tasks, and channels.

results.title: Rust Async Ecosystem Overview
results.content: The Rust async ecosystem centers around the tokio runtime, but alternatives like async-std and smol exist. Each runtime provides an executor, reactor, and various async utilities. The ecosystem also includes libraries like hyper, tonic, and tower for building network services.

results.title: tokio-rs/tokio: A runtime for writing reliable asynchronous applications with Rust
results.content: Tokio is an event-driven, non-blocking I/O platform for writing asynchronous applications with the Rust programming language. At a high level, it provides a few major components: a multithreaded work-stealing based task scheduler, a reactor backed by the operating system's event queue (epoll, kqueue, IOCP, etc), and asynchronous TCP and UDP sockets.

results.title: async-std - Async standard library for Rust
results.content: async-std is a library that provides an async version of the Rust standard library. It aims to be a drop-in replacement for std in async contexts, providing async versions of file I/O, networking, and other standard library features. It uses smol as its underlying runtime.
